Nearly 2,000 votes separate Mississippi Senate candidates
Abortion-rights advocates have achieved victories in Missouri, Nevada and Virginia

WASHINGTON -- Abortion-rights advocates notched victories in several states Tuesday, and voters delivered a double dose of disapproval to President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts as they decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states.
The ballot measures provided a political undercard for a high-profile midterm election in which Democrats took control of Congress and gained power in state legislatures and gubernatorial offices .

Some measures put Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit transgender athletes in sports and strengthen voter identification requirements.

Voters defeated a proposed amendment to Missouri’s constitution that would have reimposed restrictions on most abortions . The vote Tuesday essentially reaffirmed voters' decision from two years ago, when they became the first in the nation to undo an existing abortion ban by approving an abortion-rights amendment.

The Republican-led Legislature then referred a new, less restrictive version of an abortion ban to this year’s ballot. The measure would have allowed abortions only for medical emergencies and fetal anomalies, or in cases of rape or incest up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. It also would have amended the constitution to prohibit certain medical procedures for transgender minors.
Abortion-rights advocates, led by national progressive groups, heavily outspent abortion foes in a successful campaign to defeat the Missouri ballot measure.

In Virginia, a voter-approved measure creates a “ fundamental right to reproductive freedom ” in the state constitution, ensuring that abortions can occur during the first two trimesters of pregnancy. The amendment also creates a right to contraception and fertility care, among other things.

An amendment approved in Nevada creates a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability, which is generally considered after 21 weeks of pregnancy. The amendment won initial voter approval in 2024 but needed a second vote this year to add it to the constitution.
Since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned a nationwide right to abortion in 2022, voters in more than one-fifth of the states have passed ballot measures protecting abortion rights.

But voters in Republican-leaning Idaho on Tuesday defeated a ballot measure that would have created abortion rights in state law. Current Idaho law bans abortions unless necessary to save the life of a pregnant woman, or during the first trimester of pregnancy in cases where rape or incest has been reported to law enforcement.
Abortion-rights measures failed two years ago in Florida and South Dakota.
Nine states are using new congressional districts in the midterm elections after a rare spate of mid-decade redistricting encouraged by Trump.

In Missouri, Republican lawmakers last year adopted new House districts designed to help the GOP win an additional seat in the Kansas City area. Opponents then gathered petition signatures to put the map to a public vote.

The new districts were used in the August primary. But courts subsequently ruled they could not be used again unless first approved by voters in a November referendum. Voters put an end to the new map by rejecting the redistricting legislation on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, voters in Democratic-led Maryland approved a constitutional amendment that could pave the way for new congressional districts in the 2028 election. Democratic proponents, backed by former President Barack Obama, had urged a “yes” vote as a way to “stop Trump.”
body_zh: 2026 年选举实时结果：凯伦·巴斯 (Karen Bass) 在洛杉矶市长竞选中败给了尼西亚·拉曼 (Nithya Raman)
密西西比州参议院候选人近 2,000 张选票
堕胎权利倡导者在密苏里州、内华达州和弗吉尼亚州取得了胜利
华盛顿——周二，堕胎权倡导者在几个州取得了胜利，选民们对唐纳德·特朗普总统的选区重新划分努力表示了双倍的不满，因为他们在三打多个州决定了 145 个选区问题。
这些投票措施为备受瞩目的中期选举提供了政治底牌，民主党在这次选举中控制了国会并在州立法机构和州长办公室获得了权力。
一些措施将特朗普的优先事项置于公开测试之下，通过衡量人们对他重新划定国会选区、限制跨性别运动员参加体育运动以及加强选民身份识别要求等尝试的支持程度。
选民否决了密苏里州宪法的一项拟议修正案，该修正案将重新限制大多数堕胎。周二的投票基本上重申了选民两年前的决定，当时他们成为全国第一个通过批准堕胎权修正案来撤销现有堕胎禁令的选民。
共和党领导的立法机构随后将一项新的、限制较少的堕胎禁令提交给今年的投票。该措施仅允许在医疗紧急情况和胎儿异常、或者怀孕 12 周以内的强奸或乱伦情况下堕胎。它还将修改宪法，禁止对变性未成年人进行某些医疗程序。
由国家进步团体领导的堕胎权利倡导者在一场成功击败密苏里州投票法案的运动中比堕胎反对者投入了大量资金。
在弗吉尼亚州，一项经选民批准的措施在州宪法中确立了“生殖自由的基本权利”，确保在怀孕的前两个三个月内可以进行堕胎。该修正案还规定了避孕和生育保健等权利。
内华达州批准的一项修正案规定了在胎儿存活之前堕胎的基本权利，这通常是在怀孕 21 周后考虑的。该修正案于 2024 年赢得了初步选民的批准，但今年需要进行第二次投票才能将其添加到宪法中。
自2022年美国最高法院推翻全国范围内的堕胎权以来，超过五分之一的州的选民已经通过了保护堕胎权的投票措施。
但周二，倾向共和党的爱达荷州选民否决了一项在州法律中规定堕胎权的投票法案。爱达荷州现行法律禁止堕胎，除非为了挽救孕妇的生命而有必要，或者在怀孕的前三个月内向执法部门报告强奸或乱伦的情况。
两年前，佛罗里达州和南达科他州的堕胎权措施失败了。
在特朗普鼓励进行十年中期罕见的一连串选区重新划分之后，九个州正在中期选举中使用新的国会选区。
在密苏里州，共和党议员去年通过了新的众议院选区，旨在帮助共和党在堪萨斯城地区赢得额外席位。反对者随后收集请愿书签名，将地图进行公众投票。
新选区用于八月份的初选。但法院随后裁定，除非在 11 月的全民公投中首先得到选民的批准，否则不得再次使用它们。选民周二拒绝了重新划分选区的立法，从而结束了新地图。
与此同时，民主党领导的马里兰州选民批准了一项宪法修正案，该修正案可能为 2028 年选举中新的国会选区铺平道路。在前总统巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)的支持下，民主党支持者敦促投“赞成”票，以此作为“阻止特朗普”的一种方式。

title_en: FEMA backlog causes delays in California infrastructure projects
title_zh: FEMA backlog causes delays in California infrastructure projects
summary: FEMA is behind on approving major projects to protect Southern California from floods, earthquakes, fires and landslides.
summary_zh: FEMA is behind on approving major projects to protect Southern California from floods, earthquakes, fires and landslides.
body_en: The Federal Emergency Management Agency is behind on approving major projects to protect Southern California totaling more than $191 million, a backlog that affects projects intended to reduce damage from floods, earthquakes, fires, and landslides, according to FEMA data.

The projects are supposed to be funded by a FEMA program called Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities — or BRIC. The Government Accountability Office has been studying the BRIC program over the last year.

"Back in March of 2025, the new administration came in, and they immediately canceled the BRIC program, and what we found is there wasn't a lot of rationale behind that," said Chris Currie, the director of the GAO's Homeland Security and Justice team. "They basically said that it was wasteful at the time. When we looked at it, though, they made that decision pretty haphazardly and quickly without really thinking through any of that."
California and 19 other states sued the federal government over the cancellation of BRIC, and in the spring of 2026, a federal judge ordered FEMA to continue the program.

Despite FEMA announcing BRIC was reinstated months ago, emergency management sources tell CBS California Investigates that FEMA has not approved any pending BRIC projects in California this year, and payments on already obligated projects are slow-moving.
A GAO report released in September says the backlog of projects nationwide totals $2.2 billion.

"Inflation happened. The cost increases happened. Labor prices increased," Currie explained. "A lot of work had to be redone. In many cases, these projects couldn't continue because they were twice as expensive as they were going to be before."
Emergency management sources in California echoed those concerns, telling CBS California Investigates that some communities in the state scrapped their BRIC projects altogether due to the delays.
California has the most projects pending of any state in the country, some first submitted in 2022, including a flood control project in San Bernardino with a price tag of $15 million.
San Bernardino County declined an interview for this story, but provided a written statement to CBS California Investigates.

"We maintain a positive and productive working relationship with FEMA and Cal OES. We received initial confirmation in April that the funding was moving forward, as evidenced by the issuance of the Final Public Notice," a county spokesperson wrote in an email to CBS California Investigates. "When the County originally applied for the grant, we factored in potential cost increases five years out, and we expect the project to remain within that allocation. The project is currently in design, and we continue to advance the work, so we are positioned to move into construction once funding is received."

Some counties with projects impacted by the delays say they've had limited communication since the BRIC program went back online this year about where their projects stand and if or when any next steps should be expected.

This is happening, as some counties waiting on BRIC funds are also waiting on reimbursements for hazard mitigation funds that FEMA promised following natural disasters in those communities. Delays with those checks are putting some rural counties in a real financial bind, sources tell CBS California Investigates.
Emergency management sources say FEMA's staff covering California projects has been significantly cut down, which could cause more delays.
Currie believes the delays could leave Californians at risk.

"The longer it takes to finish a resilience project, the greater the risk, wherever that project is," Currie said. "You have to remember, I mean, the whole purpose of these projects is to reduce risk. So, if you don't implement them, or they're not done, the risk doesn't change."
In Orange County, a BRIC grant has already funded phase one of a project to build an elevated berm and vegetated sand dunes to protect a portion of Capistrano Beach from more intense flooding.
The construction phase — the phase for which FEMA is expected to pay $9,377,094 — is scheduled to begin next year, the county says.

But with FEMA's backlogs, some experts fear phase two for projects like the one in Capistrano Beach — and others in California — could take a lot longer to move forward, and with flooding battering the coast this year, moving quickly is critical.
In October, Orange County Parks acquired an additional grant to supplement the BRIC project.

title_en: Biden’s revenge: His alumni are winning in the midterms
title_zh: Biden’s revenge: His alumni are winning in the midterms
summary: The former president wasn’t a prominent force on the trail, but some of his one-time staffers have won high profile races on Tuesday night.
summary_zh: The former president wasn’t a prominent force on the trail, but some of his one-time staffers have won high profile races on Tuesday night.
body_en: Joe Biden was unceremoniously ushered out of the White House two years ago.
On Tuesday, he got a small measure of revenge.

Prominent Biden administration alumni are winning in a handful of notable races, with Keisha Lance Bottoms — the one-time Atlanta mayor turned Biden’s senior adviser and director of the Office of Public Engagement — leading the pack by flipping Georgia’s governorship.
The victories, his former staffers say, are an important part of rehabilitating his legacy within a Democratic Party that all but banished him in 2024.

“It's proof that President Biden assembled a talented team of public servants — who the public is calling on now to help turn this country around,” said Ron Klain, Biden’s former chief of staff. “These fantastic men and women will make life more affordable, health care more available, protect our rights, fight corruption, and make our country stronger.”

Biden was not a regular on the trail this year, and most Democrats kept their distance from the former president. But he did weigh in on a handful of primaries, helping put loyal lieutenants in front of voters who still held him in high regard.

While Bottoms was the highest profile victory, there’s a number of Biden alumni also poised to head to Washington. Gabe Amo, who won a 2023 special election in a blue Rhode Island seat, secured his second full term in Congress. And Dan Koh, who won Massachusetts’ 6th District to succeed Rep. Seth Moulton, was Biden’s deputy Cabinet secretary and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs.
He leaned into his Biden endorsement throughout the campaign and this week reposted a video of a phone call he and his family had with Joe and Jill Biden on primary night in September.

“Mr. President and Madame first lady, thank you so much for all of your support,” he told them. “It wouldn’t have been possible without both of you. … You changed my life by giving me a job of a lifetime. And you got my back the minute I decided to run.”

Biden’s Cabinet also had a strong night in other governor races. Xavier Becerra, Biden’s secretary of Health and Human Services, had a solid polling lead over Republican Steve Hilton in the race to be California’s next governor going into Tuesday. And, Deb Haaland, Biden’s Interior secretary, was projected to win the New Mexico governor race.

"In his farewell speech, President Biden warned that ‘an oligarchy is taking shape in America of extreme wealth, power, and influence that literally threatens our entire democracy,’” said Andrew Bates, the former president’s longtime spokesperson. “He urged his team and supporters to keep standing up for the values that we all care about, including decency, hard work, and a sense of national community. On the ballot and off, a whole lot of his alumni are fighting to carry on that legacy.”
CORRECTION: A previous version of this report misstated how many full terms Gabe Amo has served.

title_en: Bernie Sanders lost the fight in 2016. A decade later, he won the war.
title_zh: 伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 在 2016 年输掉了这场战斗。十年后，他赢得了战争。
summary: Bernie Sanders’ focus on economic populism once faced criticism within the party. Now it’s winning in Michigan, Texas, Montana and Wisconsin.
summary_zh: 伯尼·桑德斯对经济民粹主义的关注一度遭到党内批评。现在它在密歇根州、德克萨斯州、蒙大拿州和威斯康星州获胜。
body_en: In 2016, two populist revolutions threatened to remake American politics. Donald Trump’s conquered the Republican Party and delivered him the presidency. Bernie Sanders’ fell short against Hillary Clinton but introduced a populist economic vision that, at the time, much of the Democratic establishment dismissed as politically impractical.

Ten years later, Trump and MAGA were hit with a devastating midterm repudiation, as candidates across the country in blue and red states echoing versions of Sanders' message broke through in places that once seemed beyond Democrats' reach.
Sanders, as cantankerous as ever, isn’t surprised.

“If you're asking me, am I shocked by that? That the argument about economic justice and taking on oligarchs and fighting for the working class is working in Texas, is working in Ohio, is working in Montana, is working in Florida, is working all over the country — no, I am not shocked,” Sanders said in an interview Wednesday, fresh off over 20 rallies in October alone. “That is what I’ve always believed.”

Sanders’ laser focus on economic populism in 2016 faced criticism from his own party during his contentious primary against Clinton for being too dismissive of identity politics — often couched as his lack of support among Black voters. Now, his brand of relentless focus on corporate and billionaire election interventions and income inequality proved a winning formula not only for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but for James Talarico in Texas, Sam Forstag in Montana and Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin.

“Bernie normalized the kind of campaigning that really is about making a direct appeal to working people,” El Sayed told POLITICO. “Wherever I went in Michigan, there are people who remember Bernie 2016 and Bernie 2020 — we stand on the shoulders of giants.”

Given the booming results Tuesday and the breadth of wins for the left, Democrats will test whether they can avoid the same pitfalls that ultimately dogged them following their last major win in 2020 with Joe Biden’s blue-collar charm at the top of the ticket, after which the party gradually slipped back down the culture war slope.

To avoid that, Sanders said the party can do both, but that Democrats need to have the “courage” to focus on the day-to-day needs of working families, no matter what the billionaires funding the Democratic Party say.

“It's not either or. You can fight against bigotry and discrimination, but you have got to have the courage,” he said. “The courage now to say to the billionaires who are funding the Democratic Party: ‘Thank you very much for your help, but right now we are going to focus on the needs of the working families of this country, whether you like it or not.’”

Sanders’ reach is perhaps nowhere more evident than in New York City, which has emerged as the mecca of American progressivism, where Mayor Zohran Mamdani — once a Sanders-endorsed local official — is now perhaps the heir-apparent to Sanders’ progressive mantle.

The man behind Mamdani's seismic rise, progressive wunderkind Morris Katz, had more than most on the line this week. After his top client Graham Platner dropped out of the Senate race in Maine earlier this year amid scandal, Katz worked this cycle for Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Randy Villegas in California and Brian Poindexter in Ohio, while his firm, Fight Agency, worked with El-Sayed and Pennsylvania’s Bob Brooks.
The day before the election, The Atlantic published a 3,500-word piece that put “Katz’s theory of politics” on the ballot.

“A lot of people wanted to know what I’d say if we lost,” Katz said, referencing an infamous Kanye West quote Wednesday and running on 45 minutes of sleep. “I guess we’ll never know. That’s about how I feel today.”
Like Sanders, Katz sees a progressive future laser-focused on economics as the clear way forward — and nowhere is that more clear than in Texas.

“Hundreds of millions were spent against James and Gina trying to tag them on a trans issue,” he said. “It failed in epic fashion because there was no room for misunderstanding or ambiguity over what they stood for, because they had grounded themselves in such affirmative and positive economic messaging.”
“Those attacks have succeeded in the absence of an affirmative message,” he added. “Once you’re able to define yourself and provide a message, it's just a lot harder for that to work.”

It's the same formula Mamdani rode to Gracie Mansion — and, Katz argues, the lesson Democrats finally absorbed. “For a long time, politicians accepted the realities of how people felt about the economy but refused responsibility for having to take an active role in changing it,” he said. “There's no room for that anymore.”
Katz sees his and Sanders’ theory of politics as having won out across the Democratic spectrum — not just on the left flank, but among the moderates who once resisted it.

“The more moderate wing of the party has changed the definition of what a moderate is. I think that’s great,” he said. “We should be a big tent party, but you are seeing a big tent that is unified in opposition to the oligarchy, that is unified in opposition to corruption, and that is united in a pursuit of fundamental and structural change. And that’s going to be really encouraging if that can carry over to 2028.”
For Sanders, it’s vindication of an argument he's made for years and that Democrats have ignored — despite what he says is its simplicity.
body_zh: 2016年，两次民粹主义革命威胁要重塑美国政治。唐纳德·特朗普征服了共和党并让他登上了总统宝座。伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）未能与希拉里·克林顿（Hillary Clinton）抗衡，但引入了民粹主义经济愿景，当时许多民主党建制派认为这种愿景在政治上不切实际。
十年后，特朗普和 MAGA 遭受了毁灭性的中期否决，全国各地蓝州和红州的候选人呼应桑德斯的信息，在曾经看似超出民主党影响力的地方取得了突破。
一如既往的脾气暴躁的桑德斯并不感到惊讶。
“如果你问我，我对此感到震惊吗？关于经济正义、对抗寡头和为工人阶级而战的论点在德克萨斯州、俄亥俄州、蒙大拿州、佛罗里达州、全国各地都在发挥作用——不，我并不感到震惊，”桑德斯在周三接受采访时表示，仅在 10 月份就参加了 20 多场集会。 “这就是我一直相信的。”
2016年，桑德斯对经济民粹主义的高度关注在他与克林顿的争议性初选中遭到了自己所在政党的批评，因为他对身份政治过于轻视——通常被描述为他缺乏黑人选民的支持。现在，事实证明，他对企业和亿万富翁选举干预以及收入不平等的不懈关注不仅是密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·赛义德的制胜法宝，也是得克萨斯州的詹姆斯·塔拉里科、蒙大拿州的萨姆·福斯塔格和威斯康星州的丽贝卡·库克的制胜法宝。
埃尔·赛义德告诉《政治》杂志：“伯尼将真正直接吸引劳动人民的竞选活动正常化了。” “无论我走到密歇根州的哪里，都有人记得 2016 年的伯尼和 2020 年的伯尼——我们站在巨人的肩膀上。”
考虑到周二的强劲选举结果和左翼的广泛胜利，民主党将测试他们是否能够避免同样的陷阱，这些陷阱最终困扰着他们，继2020年乔·拜登的蓝领魅力占据上风后，该党逐渐滑落文化战争的斜坡。
桑德斯表示，为了避免这种情况，民主党可以两者兼顾，但民主党需要有“勇气”专注于工薪家庭的日常需求，无论资助民主党的亿万富翁怎么说。
“这不是非此即彼的问题。你可以反对偏执和歧视，但你必须有勇气，”他说。 “现在有勇气对资助民主党的亿万富翁说：‘非常感谢你们的帮助，但现在我们将重点关注这个国家工薪家庭的需求，无论你们喜欢与否。’”
桑德斯的影响力也许在纽约市最为明显，纽约已成为美国进步主义的圣地，市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼——曾经是桑德斯支持的地方官员——现在可能是桑德斯进步主义衣钵的继承人。

马姆达尼的惊人崛起背后的男人、进步神童莫里斯·卡茨(Morris Katz)本周比大多数人都面临着更大的风险。今年早些时候，卡茨的顶级客户格雷厄姆·普拉特纳 (Graham Platner) 因丑闻退出缅因州参议院竞选。此后，卡茨为德克萨斯州的吉娜·伊诺霍萨 (Gina Hinojosa)、加利福尼亚州的兰迪·维勒加斯 (Randy Villegas) 和俄亥俄州的布莱恩·波因德克斯特 (Brian Poindexter) 工作，而他的公司 Fight Agency 则与埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed) 和宾夕法尼亚州的鲍勃·布鲁克斯 (Bob Brooks) 合作。
选举前一天，《大西洋月刊》发表了一篇 3500 字的文章，将“卡茨的政治理论”列入选票。
“很多人想知道如果我们输了我会说什么，”卡茨说道，他引用了坎耶·维斯特周三的一句臭名昭著的名言，并在睡眠 45 分钟的情况下跑步。 “我想我们永远不会知道。这就是我今天的感受。”
和桑德斯一样，卡茨也认为以经济为重点的进步未来是明确的前进方向——这一点在德克萨斯州最为明显。
“人们花了数亿美元来对付詹姆斯和吉娜，试图给他们贴上跨性别者的标签，”他说。 “它以史诗般的方式失败了，因为他们所代表的东西没有任何误解或含糊的余地，因为他们以如此肯定和积极的经济信息为基础。”
“这些攻击在没有发出肯定信息的情况下取得了成功，”他补充道。 “一旦你能够定义自己并提供信息，那就很难发挥作用了。”
这与马姆达尼在格雷西大厦的做法是一样的——卡茨认为，这也是民主党最终吸取的教训。 “长期以来，政客们接受了人们对经济的看法的现实，但拒绝承担在改变经济方面发挥积极作用的责任，”他说。 “已经没有空间了。”
卡茨认为他和桑德斯的政治理论赢得了整个民主党派的支持——不仅在左翼，而且在曾经抵制它的温和派中。
“党内较为温和的一派改变了温和派的定义。我认为这很好，”他说。 “我们应该成为一个大帐篷党，但你看到的是一个大帐篷，它团结起来反对寡头政治，团结起来反对腐败，团结起来追求根本性和结构性变革。如果这种情况能够延续到 2028 年，那将是非常令人鼓舞的。”
对于桑德斯来说，这证明了他多年来提出的一个论点是正确的，而民主党却忽视了这一论点——尽管他说这个论点很简单。

title_en: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
title_zh: OpenAI 退出数据中心项目的 NDA
summary: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements
summary_zh: 继本周的中期选举中选民强烈反对数据中心扩建之后，OpenAI 今天宣布了新的承诺：
body_en: The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.
Jay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers ) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

body_en: President Trump said Thursday night that voters had themselves to blame for the stock market's historic sell-off .
Why it matters: Two days after Republicans lost the midterm elections in historic fashion, the president is lashing out at the voters who rejected his candidates and message.
Driving the news: Stocks plunged Thursday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq sinking more than 5% as AI-linked stocks sold off.
Investors are skittish about the future for AI development — and the data centers that power the technology — after Tuesday's blue wave ushered in candidates who campaigned on restricting AI.
What he's saying: " The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!" Trump posted to Truth Social.
The intrigue: Thursday's plunge was an unusually delayed reaction — the market actually had a massive rally Wednesday as the initial election results became apparent.
Trump was quick to claim credit at the time for the conditions that led to those market highs.
What to watch: Stock futures were down again in pre-market trading late Thursday, and Asian markets were broadly lower as well, pointing to the potential for another rough day Friday.
body_zh: 特朗普总统周四晚间表示，股市历史性抛售应归咎于选民自己。
为什么重要：共和党以历史性方式输掉中期选举两天后，总统猛烈抨击那些拒绝他的候选人和信息的选民。
推动这一消息的是：周四股市暴跌，随着人工智能相关股票遭到抛售，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌超过 5%。
在周二的蓝色浪潮迎来了限制人工智能的候选人之后，投资者对人工智能发展的未来以及为该技术提供动力的数据中心感到不安。
他的意思是：“今天股市崩盘，因为杜民主党度过了一个重要的星期二——看到如此令人难过，只能怪你们自己！”特朗普在真相社交网站上发帖。
阴谋：周四的暴跌是一种异常延迟的反应——随着初步选举结果的显现，市场实际上在周三出现了大幅反弹。
特朗普当时很快就将导致市场高点的条件归功于自己。
看点：周四晚间盘前交易中，股指期货再次下跌，亚洲市场也普遍走低，这表明周五可能又会出现艰难的一天。

title_en: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
title_zh: 对中期选举后人工智能打击的担忧引发科技股暴跌 2 万亿美元
summary: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.

body_en: Stocks sink as AI fears build after midterms : NPR

Stocks sink as AI fears build after midterms Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.

Stocks sank as investors fear an incoming Democratic Congress — and states across the country — could crack down on the AI industry and data centers. Timothy A. Clary/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Two days after Democrats won overwhelmingly in the national midterm elections — and in state races across the country — investors started to come to terms with the potential consequences.
6 takeaways from Democrats' big wave on election night
Fears that an incoming Democratic Congress would crack down on AI sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq down more than 5% and wiped out more than $2 trillion in market value. The Dow Jones and S&P also sank.
The losses were a stark reversal from Wednesday, when investors had initially sent shares higher across the board, relieved that the midterms did not end with the fate of Congress undecided.
How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio

The sobering-up seen across markets on Thursday reflected investors' concern about a big signal sent by voters: They revolted against AI data centers , which many people worry will gobble up water and energy resources. Those voters supported Democrats who have vowed to push back against the proliferation of these projects.
But many AI companies — including Meta and Alphabet, the parent company of Google — need to keep building out these data centers to continue developing the technology.

The Nasdaq's decline comes after what has already been a rough year of technology shares on Wall Street, with investors starting to question whether the massive investments companies have plowed into AI will pay off anytime soon.

"There is some concern regarding AI regulation, and fears that there could be far more regulations coming to AI technology, as well as a pushback on the buildout of data centers across the country," says David Busch, chief investment officer of Trajan Wealth.

AI-related or AI-dependent stocks of all kinds were among the biggest decliners on Thursday, with Tesla and SpaceX — both controlled by billionaire Elon Musk — falling particularly sharply. Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars in an unsuccessful attempt to elect more Republicans, and investors fear he and his companies could also come under Democratic scrutiny when the new Congress is seated in January.
The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
It's not only Congress, however. Democrats who vowed to slow down AI development also won at the state level, most prominently Gina Hinojosa, who won the Texas governor's race in stunning fashion.

It's unclear whether the AI stock rout will continue — or spread beyond tech stocks. AI has become a big driver of the U.S. economy, helping it post a solid annual growth of 3.4% in the July-September quarter.

And sophisticated Wall Street investors are not the only ones who own a lot of shares in AI companies. Average Americans also own them through their retirement investment portfolios — such as 401(k)s or pension funds — leaving them also vulnerable to a prolonged AI rout.

body_zh: 随着人工智能恐慌在中期选举后加剧，股市下跌： NPR
随着人工智能担忧在中期股价下跌后加剧，股市下跌，科技股重量级纳斯达克指数下跌超过5% ，投资者担心民主党国会--以及全国各州-—将打击人工智能和数据中心。
由于投资者担心即将上任的民主党国会以及全国各州可能会打击人工智能行业和数据中心，股市下跌。 Timothy A. Clary/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
民主党在全国中期选举以及全国州竞选中以压倒性优势获胜两天后，投资者开始接受潜在的后果。
选举之夜民主党大浪潮的 6 个要点
由于担心即将上任的民主党国会将严厉打击人工智能，导致以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数下跌超过 5%，市值蒸发超过 2 万亿美元。道琼斯指数和标准普尔指数也下跌。
这些损失与周三的情况截然不同，当时投资者最初推高股价，因为中期选举并未因国会命运未决而结束，这让他们松了一口气。
一位终身共和党人如何领导俄亥俄州数据中心之战
周四市场的清醒反映了投资者对选民发出的一个重大信号的担忧：他们反对人工智能数据中心，许多人担心人工智能数据中心会吞噬水资源和能源。这些选民支持民主党人，他们发誓要阻止这些项目的扩散。
但许多人工智能公司——包括 Meta 和谷歌母公司 Alphabet——需要继续建设这些数据中心以继续开发技术。
纳斯达克指数的下跌是在华尔街科技股经历了艰难的一年之后发生的，投资者开始质疑公司在人工智能领域的大规模投资是否会很快得到回报。
Trajan Wealth 首席投资官 David Busch 表示：“人们对人工智能监管存在一些担忧，担心人工智能技术可能会受到更多监管，以及全国范围内数据中心建设的阻力。”
周四，各种与人工智能相关或依赖人工智能的股票跌幅最大，其中特斯拉和 SpaceX（均由亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克控制）跌幅尤其严重。马斯克花费了数亿美元试图选举更多共和党人，但没有成功，投资者担心，当新一届国会在一月份就座时，他和他的公司也可能受到民主党的审查。
韩国在中期选举中展示政治权力，在 2028 年选举中确定地区影响力
然而，这不仅仅是国会。发誓要减缓人工智能发展的民主党人也在州一级获胜，其中最著名的是吉娜·伊诺霍萨(Gina Hinojosa)，她以惊人的方式赢得了德克萨斯州州长的竞选。
目前尚不清楚人工智能股的暴跌是否会持续下去，或者蔓延到科技股之外。人工智能已成为美国经济的重要推动力，帮助美国在 7 月至 9 月季度实现了 3.4% 的稳健年增长率。
成熟的华尔街投资者并不是唯一拥有大量人工智能公司股票的人。普通美国人还通过退休投资组合（例如 401(k) 或养老基金）拥有它们，这使得他们也容易受到人工智能长期溃败的影响。
